site.name: aurora-network
site.summary: Aurora Network — Privacy & Audience (local demo) Fictional social network. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly in a browser. Pages `index.html` — Privacy overview Entry hub. Four cards (Default audience, Tag review, Past post visibility, Muted words) link to each privacy-management surface. Below the cards, a "Snapshot" panel summarizes the user's current privacy state as a key/value list. `audience.html` — Default audience Radio-group selector with four options (Public, Friends, Custom list, Only me). Below the selector: dynamic explanation of who can see new posts, custom-list manager (create / inspect / view recent use), and a "Who can tag you?" radio block. `tag-review.html` — Pending tag queue

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore Aurora Network's privacy and audience settings flow, with emphasis on the overview hub, default audience configuration, tag review queue, past post visibility bulk actions, and muted words management, including mobile usability checks.
run_plan.summary: Start from the Privacy & Audience overview to map how the four privacy surfaces connect and to verify the snapshot panel reflects navigation targets. Then validate each dedicated page in turn, exercising the visible controls and confirming state/explanation changes where the UI suggests them. Treat bulk/privacy-impacting controls as high risk, and repeat the critical interactions on mobile because the prescan shows multiple small tap targets across the settings pages.
assumptions: The four privacy cards on index.html are the primary entry points and should lead to the dedicated pages listed in the prescan.
The site is a local demo with no backend side effects, but the UI may still simulate state changes, counts, and summaries.
The only known pages are the five HTML files in the prescan; no hidden flows should be assumed beyond the visible controls.
Mobile validation should focus on tap-target sizing and whether the dense sidebar/card layout remains usable at narrow widths.
risk_hotspots: index.html snapshot panel and 'Change' links: verify they point to the intended privacy surfaces and do not create confusing duplicate paths.
audience.html radio groups for default audience and 'Who can tag you?': privacy-sensitive state changes and multiple options with explanatory text.
audience.html custom list manager / New list controls: check for discoverability, list handling, and whether the 'last used list' behavior is understandable.
tag-review.html 'Approve all' and 'Hide all': high-impact batch actions on pending tags.
tag-review.html per-item Approve / Hide tag / Block user actions: verify individual review outcomes and whether counts or queue state update coherently.
past-posts.html year/audience filters and 'Apply to visible': bulk historical visibility changes with irreversible implications called out by the overview.
blocked-words.html add-word input, Mute action, Import .txt / Export .txt, and removable phrase chips: list-editing and file-style actions are likely to be error-prone.
Mobile viewport across all pages: the prescan already reports multiple small tap targets, especially in the nav/sidebar.

phases.title: Map the privacy hub
phases.objective: Confirm index.html acts as the central privacy hub and that the four feature cards and snapshot links route correctly.
key_checks: Open each of the four privacy cards from the hub: Default audience, Tag review, Past post visibility, and Muted words.
Click the inline 'Change' links in the snapshot panel and verify they lead to the expected destination page or reveal any mismatch.
Note whether the snapshot values visually correspond to the current state described in the cards.
Check whether the left nav and top nav create duplicate or confusing entry points.
exit_criteria: All known privacy entry points from the hub have been visited or confirmed.
Any mismatched or redundant links from the snapshot/overview are identified.
The relationship between the overview and the four subpages is understood well enough to proceed.

phases.title: Validate default audience and tagging rules
phases.objective: Exercise the main audience selection flow and inspect the adjacent custom list and tag-permission controls on audience.html.
key_checks: Cycle through the visible audience radio options: Public, Friends, Custom list, and Only me.
Observe the dynamic explanation text for each selection and confirm it changes in a way that matches the chosen audience.
Inspect the custom list section, including the New list control and the visible lists/usage hints, for clarity and obvious interactive affordances.
Check the 'Who can tag you?' radio block and confirm it is distinct from the default audience setting.
If Save default and Discard changes are active, test both flows to confirm whether unsaved changes are handled consistently.
exit_criteria: Every visible audience option has been selected at least once.
The tag-permission controls and custom list area have been inspected for state/feedback behavior.
Any save/discard behavior has been validated or confirmed absent.

phases.title: Review pending tags
phases.objective: Test the moderation queue and batch/individual actions on tag-review.html.
key_checks: Verify the queue count (7 pending) matches the list content shown on the page.
Test the page-level actions Approve all and Hide all, if they are enabled, and note how the queue changes afterward.
For several individual items, exercise Approve, Hide tag, and Block user to confirm each action has distinct feedback or state impact.
Check whether the UI makes it clear that pending tags remain visible in the original post even when the profile tag is hidden.
exit_criteria: At least one batch action and several per-item actions have been tested.
The distinction between approving a tag and hiding/blocking it is clear from observed behavior.
The queue/count behavior is validated for consistency.

phases.title: Audit historical post restrictions
phases.objective: Exercise the bulk historical visibility sweep and the filtering controls on past-posts.html.
key_checks: Change the year filter and audience filter to confirm they narrow the visible posts as expected.
Inspect the per-post Edit actions to understand whether the page supports item-level changes as well as bulk changes.
Use Apply to visible after selecting a filter combination and observe whether the selected visible posts are affected together.
Verify that the page communicates the bulk-action risk described on the overview, especially that it is a sweeping historical change.
exit_criteria: Both filtering dimensions have been used.
The bulk apply control has been tested against a visible subset.
The page's historical privacy implications are confirmed to be clearly signposted or not.

phases.title: Stress-test muted words management
phases.objective: Validate phrase management on blocked-words.html, including add/remove and import/export behaviors.
key_checks: Add at least one new phrase via the input and Mute action, then verify whether it appears in the list.
Remove one or more existing muted words via the chip delete controls to check deletion clarity and undo absence/presence.
Inspect Import .txt and Export .txt for discoverability and any obvious state changes or prompts.
Review the scope/explanation section to confirm where muted words apply and whether exceptions are understandable.
If duration or other settings are exposed below the fold, scroll to confirm they are present and accessible.
exit_criteria: List add/remove behavior has been exercised.
Import/export controls have been opened or tested enough to confirm their role.
Scope/exemption text has been reviewed for clarity.

phases.title: Mobile usability pass
phases.objective: Repeat the most important interactions in a mobile viewport and confirm the dense privacy UI remains operable.
key_checks: Revisit the overview and the four privacy pages at mobile width, with special attention to the small-tap-target warnings.
Check whether the sidebar/nav items, top nav, and action controls remain reachable without overlap or accidental taps.
Repeat one high-risk action per page on mobile: open a card from the hub, change an audience option, act on one tag, adjust a filter/apply action, and add/remove a muted word.
Note any layout shifts that hide content, truncate labels, or make the card grid/side nav difficult to use.
exit_criteria: Critical interactions have been repeated on mobile for the key pages.
Any mobile-specific failures or usability degradations have been captured.
Coverage is sufficient to compare desktop vs mobile behavior for the main privacy flows.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages in the prescan: index.html, audience.html, tag-review.html, past-posts.html, and blocked-words.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the primary controls on each page: overview card navigation, audience radio choices, tag review batch and per-item moderation, past-posts filters plus bulk apply, and muted words add/remove/import/export.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the most important interactions on a mobile viewport and explicitly check the small tap targets, navigation reachability, and layout stability.

notes: The prescan shows low-severity small tap target warnings across the shell and settings nav; do not treat these as isolated to one page.
Avoid assuming any functionality outside the visible controls and the five known pages.
Because the overview warns that historical changes cannot be undone in bulk, give extra attention to the past-posts apply flow.

ux_notes: Clicking Apply to visible opened a modal confirmation, so the bulk action is clearly signposted before execution.
The confirmation explains scope in plain language: it affects every visible post above, estimating about 8 posts.
The dialog also states the change is not reversible in bulk and requires individual reopening to widen audience again.
A visible Cancel option is present alongside the destructive confirm button, supporting safe cancellation.

step.objective: Learn whether the destructive bulk visibility action executes with clear feedback and whether the result state is understandable on mobile.
step.success_criteria: The modal should close and the page should show a clear updated state/count or confirmation that the visible posts were changed, revealing how the destructive action is communicated after execution.

result.feedback: Visible content changed after the action.

The current state is only partially understandable: the page still shows '8 visible posts' and the filtered post list, but the destructive action's effect is not explicitly confirmed in the UI.

step.objective: Learn whether a final interaction on the mobile past-posts page or adjacent control reveals additional UX feedback beyond the bulk flow already tested.
step.success_criteria: New content or footer/state should become visible, confirming whether the page offers additional controls, feedback, or recovery information below the current fold.
